basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 13.' and it opens '(Vers. 13.) Et viri Sodomorum mali et peccatores in conspectu Dei vehementer. Superflue'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 13.) Et viri Sodomorum mali et peccatores in conspectu Dei vehementer. Superflue hic in Septuaginta Interpretibus additum est, in conspectu Dei, siquidem Sodomorum coloni apud homines [Al. omnes], mali et peccatores erant. Ille autem dicitur in conspectu Dei peccator, qui potest apud homines justus videri, quomodo de Zacharia et Elizabeth in praeconio ponitur, quod fuerint justi ambo in conspectu Dei (Luc. I, 6). Et in Psalterio dicitur: Non justificabitur in conspectu tuo omnis vivens (Ps. CXLII, 2).
